rows.question: At reset of floating rates, does a UCB have to give borrowers a choice to switch to a fixed rate?
rows.answer: A UCB is not required to offer borrowers a choice to switch to a fixed rate at the reset of floating interest rates, because the applicable UCB rule says it may, at its option, provide that choice as per its Board-approved policy. The same UCB rule also treats the fixed-rate switch as one of the options that may be provided at reset, rather than as a mandatory offer. A superseded 2025 reset circular also used permissive wording, stating that the bank may, at its option, offer the borrower a choice to switch to a fixed rate.

rows.question: Since RBI now allows penal interest to be capitalised, how often may we compound it?
rows.answer: For this UCB, penal charges may not be capitalised, so there is no permitted compounding frequency for penal interest or penal charges.  The current directions say there must be no capitalization of the penal charges, meaning no further interest is computed on those charges.  They also say additional or fresh penal charges shall not be levied on the earlier outstanding amount of penal charges.  The older 2023 circulars that mentioned normal procedures for compounding of interest are superseded and no longer in force.
